clue.text: Wine with queen getting excited

blocks.note: Asti is an Italian sparkling wine
R, for Regina, is the standard abbreviation for queen

explanation.surface: A monarch gets giddy after a glass or two.
explanation.definitionFit: Astir means up and moving about, in a state of commotion, which is a synonym for excited.

clue.text: Settle in car seat, wriggling

indicators.note: something wriggling twists about, so these letters squirm into another order

blocks.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A fidgety child getting comfortable in the back of the car.
explanation.definitionFit: To ascertain is to find out for certain, to settle a question or fact beyond doubt.

clue.text: Knocks by back of cricket nets

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter

blocks.note: the last letter of this word
raps are sharp knocks

explanation.surface: A batsman takes blows at net practice, where cricketers train inside netted lanes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' lets the knocks sit beside the letter, here after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Traps and nets are both devices for catching animals, so the plural nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: Went to bed about worn out

blocks.note: re means about or concerning
tired means worn out

explanation.surface: An exhausted person turned in for the night.
explanation.definitionFit: Retired is a formal way of saying someone withdrew for the night, i.e. went to sleep.

clue.text: Rendered insensible from drink

blocks.note: first meaning: coated with a layer of render, as a wall is
second meaning: slang for very drunk

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one phrase, 'rendered insensible', but 'Rendered' is a separate builder's sense: render is a cement coating for walls.
explanation.definitionFit: A plastered wall has been given a smooth coat, and plastered is also everyday slang for heavily intoxicated.

clue.text: Victorians, bawdy with empty pious exterior

definitions.note: used loosely for people with strict Victorian morals

indicators.note: an empty word has lost its middle, so only its outside letters remain
an exterior is the outside shell wrapped round the other part

blocks.note: the first and last letters of this word
bawdy jokes are rude ones

explanation.surface: Nineteenth-century folk who were smutty underneath a hollow show of religion.
explanation.definitionFit: Victorians, in the figurative sense, are strait-laced moralists who are easily shocked, just as prudes are.

clue.text: Hatred is over and practically beaten

indicators.note: practically means nearly all, so the word loses its last letter
beaten as in whisked, so the letters are mixed up together

blocks.note: taken as written
this word with its final letter dropped

explanation.surface: Loathing ends once a foe is all but defeated.
explanation.definitionFit: An aversion is a strong dislike or disinclination, close to hatred.

clue.text: Rubbish lampblack promoted for ink?

definitions.note: ink is slang for tattoos collectively; the question mark flags the informal sense

indicators.note: in a down entry, promoted means moved upward, so the word is read from bottom to top

blocks.note: tat is cheap, shoddy goods
lampblack is a fine soot

explanation.surface: Junk soot being sold as writing ink.
explanation.walkthrough: TAT is British for junk or trinkets.
explanation.definitionFit: Having 'ink' is modern slang for having body art, so the word stands for tattoos generally.

clue.text: Recover crew's core — gang on ship
Embellishment of French gold covering clubs

indicators.note: the outer words cover the other by wrapping round it

blocks.note: de is French for of
C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A French gold leaf decorating golf clubs or playing cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Decor is the decorative style and furnishings of a room, i.e. its ornamentation or embellishment.

clue.text: Each tune's different for female singer

indicators.note: something different has been changed, so the letters before it are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A singer gives every song a fresh twist.
explanation.definitionFit: Chanteuse is the French-borrowed word for a woman who sings, especially in a nightclub or cabaret.

clue.text: Crown in charge for subject

blocks.note: the crown of something is its top
IC is the usual abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: Who wears the crown and runs the state is under discussion.
explanation.definitionFit: A topic is a theme or matter of discussion, a synonym for subject.

clue.text: Order dish up again

blocks.note: first meaning: to book in advance
second meaning: read as RE- plus serve, to serve food a second time

explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a diner asking for a second helping; the second sense splits the word into re- and serve.
explanation.definitionFit: To reserve a table is to book or order it ahead, and re-serving food means putting it out once more.

clue.text: Trail taking opposite points back

indicators.note: a word that takes something in holds it inside itself

blocks.note: spoor is the track or scent left by an animal
north and south are opposite compass points

explanation.surface: A hiker follows a path that doubles back on itself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' looks like part of the trail picture, as in going back, but it is the definition, in the sense of support.
explanation.definitionFit: To sponsor a cause or person is to support it financially, which is what backing someone means.

clue.text: File a nail with file, finally

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word before it

blocks.note: taken as written
a brad is a thin flat-headed nail
the last letter of this word

explanation.surface: A manicure instruction: smooth one fingernail with an emery board to finish.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes the nail a fingernail; here it is the carpenter's kind, a brad.
explanation.definitionFit: To abrade is to wear down by rubbing, which is what filing a surface does.

clue.text: Left sweetheart first wearing wedding band

indicators.note: the band is worn around the letters, enclosing them

blocks.note: the heart of 'sweet' is its central letter
main means chief or first
a wedding band is a ring

explanation.surface: A jilted partner abandons their beloved but still wears the ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweetheart' looks like a lover, but it is split: the heart of 'sweet'.
explanation.definitionFit: Remaining and left both mean still there after the rest has gone, as in 'two cakes left'.

clue.text: Terrible row as ref gives kick

indicators.note: something terrible is in a bad state, so these letters are messed up into a new order

blocks.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A football referee awards a free kick after an awful argument on the pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kick' sits in a football picture, but it is the verb in the sense of giving up a habit, as in kicking smoking.
explanation.definitionFit: To forswear something is to renounce or abandon it, just as to kick a habit is to quit it.

clue.text: Pore over skirt being forward?

blocks.note: to pore over a text is to read it closely
a skirt is part of a dress, loosely a dress

explanation.surface: Studying a short skirt and finding it rather bold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forward' suggests boldness; it is the postal verb, and the question mark admits the stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: To forward a letter to a new address is to readdress it, putting a fresh destination on the envelope.

clue.text: Chatted, never getting upset about rivalry

indicators.note: about here means the letters are strewn across the run of words, sitting inside them
in a down entry, upset means turned upside down, so the letters read from bottom to top

blocks.note: the tail of the first word joined to the start of the second

explanation.surface: Two people who talk constantly but never fall out over their rivalry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chatted' and 'never' look like wordplay to be converted into synonyms, but the letters are already there, read backwards across the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A vendetta is a prolonged bitter feud between parties, an intense form of rivalry.

clue.text: Refusals to accept explosive candidates

indicators.note: the outer word accepts the other into its middle, enclosing it

blocks.note: noes are negative answers or votes
a mine is an explosive device

explanation.surface: Volatile election hopefuls get turned down.
explanation.definitionFit: Nominees are people put forward for election or an award, which is what candidates are.

clue.text: Somebody generous accepts thanks

indicators.note: the outer word accepts the other into itself

blocks.note: noble can mean magnanimous or generous
ta is British informal for thanks

explanation.surface: A big-hearted person graciously receives gratitude.
explanation.definitionFit: A notable, as a noun, is an important person, which is what a 'somebody' is as opposed to a nobody.

clue.text: Female entertainer in lounge is harmonising

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the run of words that follows

blocks.note: found running across the end of lounge, all of is and the start of harmonising

explanation.surface: A singer performs in a hotel bar, adding harmonies.
explanation.definitionFit: A geisha is a Japanese woman trained to entertain guests with music, dance and conversation.

clue.text: Cuts taxes

blocks.note: first meaning: removes surgically or edits out, a verb
second meaning: duties levied on goods, a plural noun

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a headline about tax cuts; the two words are separate senses, one a verb and one a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: To excise is to cut out, and excises are also duties charged on goods such as alcohol and tobacco.

clue.text: Fancy talk about Republican's end

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter
about means around, so one piece goes around the other

blocks.note: to orate is to speak formally
the last letter of Republican

explanation.surface: Elaborate speeches concerning the end of a Republican presidency.
explanation.definitionFit: Ornate means elaborately decorated, which is what fancy means as an adjective.

clue.text: Wooden ship's prow listed

indicators.note: a prow is the front of a vessel, so take the first letter of the word

blocks.note: the front letter of this word
a ship that lists leans to one side, i.e. tilts

explanation.surface: The front of a timber ship leaned over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wooden' looks like a description of the ship, but it is the definition in the sense of stiff and awkward.
explanation.definitionFit: Stilted speech or acting is stiff and unnatural, which is what wooden means of a performance.

clue.text: Bags maybe producing sound of instrument

indicators.note: the sound of a word means we want something spoken the same way

blocks.note: a sax is a saxophone

explanation.surface: Bagpipes perhaps, making a musical noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bags' suggests bagpipes alongside 'instrument'; here it simply defines by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Sacks are large bags, so bags are an example of the answer, flagged by 'maybe'.

clue.text: Grass protecting copper's removed from case

indicators.note: something protecting another wraps around it, so one word goes round the other

blocks.note: a reed is a tall grass
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper, plus the S of the possessive

explanation.surface: An informer shielding a police officer is taken off the investigation.
explanation.walkthrough: In the surface a grass is an informer and a copper a policeman; the wordplay wants a plant and a metal.
explanation.definitionFit: A judge who recuses themselves withdraws from hearing a case because of a conflict of interest.

clue.text: Show merriment in lips' elevation, initially

definitions.text: Show merriment in lips' elevation, initially

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of each word before it

blocks.note: the opening letters of these five words

explanation.surface: Raising the corners of one's mouth to express amusement.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: the first letters spell the answer and the clue describes it.
explanation.definitionFit: A smile is an upward curve of the lips that shows pleasure or amusement.

clue.text: Rise of Conservative member

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative
a member is a limb of the body

explanation.surface: A Tory MP's career takes off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'member' suggests a member of parliament, but it is an arm or leg.
explanation.definitionFit: A climb is an ascent, an upward slope or movement, a noun synonym for a rise.

clue.text: Come out and partner is upset!

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disturbed, so the letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone comes out to their other half, who takes it badly.
explanation.definitionFit: When a fact transpires it becomes known or emerges, which is to say it comes out.

clue.text: Isolate hollow sample, say, in jar

indicators.note: a hollow word has had its insides removed, leaving only its first and last letters
in says the abbreviation goes inside the following word

blocks.note: the outside letters of this word
to jar is to grate, as on the nerves
e.g. means for example, i.e. say

explanation.surface: A lab instruction: keep an empty specimen in a container on its own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jar' reads as a container but is the verb, to grate.
explanation.definitionFit: To segregate is to set apart from others, which is a synonym for isolate.

clue.text: Looks of male covered in spots

indicators.note: a thing covered in another is wrapped inside it

blocks.note: M is the abbreviation for male
to spot something is to see it

explanation.surface: A man's appearance when his face breaks out in pimples.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Looks' and 'spots' both read as nouns about a face; both are verbs.
explanation.definitionFit: Seems and looks are both verbs for appearing to be, as in 'he looks tired'.
